A. Complete the table to show where the places are.

The first one has been done for you.

| Places | Grid Square |
| :--- | :--- |
| Playground | B2 |
| School | |
| Corner of Maple and Oak Streets | |

[Image: a map with the x-axis labeled A to F from left to right and the y-axis labeled 1 to 4 from down to up on a grid with various squares labeled Playground, Library, Shop, and Fire Station.]

descriptors: Both the places are correct: School (F2) AND Maple/Oak Streets (E3). Do not accept 2F or 3E.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

figure_description: A 6-by-4 grid with columns labeled A, B, C, D, E, F from left to right along the bottom, and rows labeled 1, 2, 3, 4 from bottom to top along the left. A network of wide gray roads runs through the grid: a main horizontal road runs through row 3 from column A to F; from it, a road angles upward into D4, and a vertical road runs downward through column E down to row 1. Another horizontal road segment runs across row 2 from column C through column F, with a small downward branch to square C1. Several grid squares contain illustrated locations: square B2 contains two children on a seesaw, labeled "Playground"; square C1 contains a building labeled "Library"; square E1 contains a store labeled "Shop"; square F2 contains a school building with a bell tower; square F4 contains a building labeled "Fire Station".
